transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, hi, thanks. I guess the main reason I’m here is I’ve been making these really stupid mistakes at work, and it’s starting to worry me. I supervise a sales team, so I have to deal with reports and procedures and checking things over, and lately I’ll think I’ve reviewed something carefully, but then later I find out I copied the wrong numbers from the team dashboard into a sales report, or I missed a line in a procedure I was supposed to verify.

It’s not like I don’t care or I’m trying to rush through it. That’s what’s frustrating. I’ll sit there and feel like, okay, I went over this, I checked it, and then someone points out that a number is off or that I skipped something obvious. And it feels embarrassing because these are the kinds of details I’m supposed to be on top of. It’s happened enough that I figured I should talk to someone rather than just keep telling myself to “try harder,” because I am trying, but it’s still happening.
Have you noticed these kinds of careless mistakes and concentration problems since childhood or adolescence, or is this something that started more recently as an adult?

Yeah, no, this definitely isn’t brand new. I mean, the work stuff is what finally made me come in because now there are consequences and people notice, but when I think back, I was kind of like this as a kid too.

My mom still brings it up sometimes, actually. She’ll talk about notes teachers sent home from elementary school, like that I rushed through assignments and made mistakes I shouldn’t have, or I’d lose homework even if I had done it. And I guess I talked out of turn a lot too, like blurting things out, and I had trouble staying in my seat unless the teacher kept reminding me. At the time I think people just treated it like I was being careless or needed to “settle down,” but yeah, looking back, it sounds pretty similar.
Outside of work, do you notice these same kinds of concentration slips, restlessness, or impulsive moments—like at home, in relationships, or during other daily activities?

Yeah, it definitely shows up outside work too. Honestly, that’s part of why I’m embarrassed, because it’s not just some office paperwork thing.

Like, I’ll forget regular life stuff that I really should not be forgetting. I’ve had calls I was supposed to return to my attorney, and I’ll think, “Okay, I need to call them back after lunch,” and then somehow the whole day goes by, then another day, and suddenly I’m realizing I never did it. Or bills—I don’t mean that I don’t have the money set aside necessarily, it’s more like I just don’t follow through on the actual paying part until a late notice shows up, and then I’m mad at myself because it was avoidable.

And with my kids, that one bothers me the most. I’ll tell them I’m going to pick something up for them, like something they need or something I promised to bring home, and then I’ll get home and realize I completely forgot. Then I have to see their faces and it feels awful, because it comes across like I didn’t care enough to remember, but in my head I did care. I just… it slips. So yeah, it’s definitely in daily life too, not just at work.
Have you been experiencing any persistent low mood, loss of interest, or excessive worry/anxiety that might be affecting your concentration, separate from these attention and organization issues?

I’m not totally sure how to separate it, honestly. I wouldn’t say I’ve been walking around with this constant low mood or like I’ve lost interest in everything. I still care about my kids, my work, stuff I normally care about. I do get frustrated with myself, definitely, and sometimes I feel pretty embarrassed when I miss something obvious, but that feels more like a reaction to messing up than the starting point.

As far as worry, I mean… I worry about the mistakes after they happen, or I’ll worry I’m going to forget something again because I’ve done it before. But I don’t know that I’d call it this constant anxiety that’s driving the concentration problems. It feels more like my attention slips first, and then the stress comes afterward when I’m dealing with the consequences.
These days, do you notice things like feeling restless or fidgety, having trouble sitting still through meetings, or blurting things out or interrupting people in conversations?

Yeah, the restlessness part is definitely there. Meetings are probably the easiest example. If it’s a short meeting, I can usually get through it, but when it’s one of those long ones where everyone’s going around in circles, it feels like my body is buzzing on the inside. Like I’m sitting there trying to look normal, but I’m shifting in the chair, crossing and uncrossing my legs, tapping my foot, messing with a pen, whatever.

And it’s not even always that I’m trying to be rude or leave. It’s more like I get this pressure building up, like I need to move. Sometimes I’ll make an excuse to get up—go refill my water, use the bathroom, check on something—just so I’m not stuck in the chair anymore. I’ve caught myself doing that even when I don’t really need to go anywhere. It just feels better to stand up or walk for a second.

Have you ever had distinct periods—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, and had racing thoughts or a surge of energy, separate from your everyday restlessness?

I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had days where I’m more keyed up or irritable, sure, especially if there’s a lot going on, but not like a whole separate stretch of days where I’m suddenly euphoric or running on no sleep and feeling amazing or anything like that.

The sleep thing especially—if I don’t sleep enough, I usually feel it. I’m not one of those people who can just sleep three hours and then feel supercharged for days. And racing thoughts… I mean, my mind jumps around a lot, but that feels like my usual thing, not some big episode where everything changes and I’m full of energy or acting like a different person.

So, no, I haven’t really noticed distinct periods like that. At least not in the way you’re describing.
